scenes.voiceover: Who sends India the most money? For the first time ever, it's not the Gulf.
scenes.image_prompt: Hook question with currency symbols floating above globe showing India and Middle East

scenes.voiceover: A hundred and forty-five billion dollars. India just smashed its remittance record — up sixteen percent in a single year.
scenes.image_prompt: Giant $145 BILLION number with upward trend chart showing FY24-FY26 growth

scenes.voiceover: America now leads at twenty-eight percent. UAE dropped to nineteen. UK, Saudi, Singapore round out the top five.
scenes.image_prompt: Horizontal bar chart showing US 27.7%, UAE 19.2%, UK 10.8%, Saudi 6.7%, Singapore 6.6%

scenes.voiceover: Why the shift? Fewer Gulf laborers. More tech workers and doctors in the US and UK. Bigger paychecks, bigger transfers.
scenes.image_prompt: Split screen showing Gulf construction workers fading vs tech professionals in modern offices

scenes.voiceover: Even with war in West Asia, Q4 hit fourteen billion a month. NRIs sent more, not less.
scenes.image_prompt: Rising green chart line breaking through chaos of West Asia conflict imagery

scenes.voiceover: It's beyond wire transfers now. NRIs buy property, invest in mutual funds, earn seven percent on dollar deposits.
scenes.image_prompt: Three investment panels: real estate, mutual fund SIPs, FCNR deposits at 7%

scenes.voiceover: Five million Indians in America. Their money home outweighs most foreign aid programs. The diaspora isn't just sending love — it's powering an economy.
scenes.image_prompt: Indian and American flags connected by golden light, text about 5 million Indians
